technical.lead: Alibaba takes Qwen3.8-Max generally available, open weights promised next week
technical.body: Qwen3.8-Max went generally available today, the largest model Alibaba has shipped under the Qwen name: 2.4 trillion total parameters with roughly 95 billion active per token, a sparse mixture-of-experts layout paired with a hybrid attention scheme meant to keep latency and compute under what a dense model of that size would demand. It takes text, images and video, returns text, and carries a listed context window of a million tokens. Arena's leaderboards place it second on Vision Arena and fourth on Frontend Code Arena, and Alibaba pitches it on autonomous coding and long-horizon agent work. The API is priced at two dollars per million input tokens and six dollars per million output. The part that reaches anyone running models on their own hardware is not the flagship but what Alibaba says arrives next week: the open weights, plus a smaller Qwen3.8-27B released alongside them. That would put a frontier-scale Chinese model and a workstation-scale sibling into the same release window.

technical.lead: Project Perception opens to the public inside Microsoft Defender
technical.body: The public-preview date Microsoft set when it introduced Project Perception a week ago arrived today, and the system is now open inside Microsoft Defender. It coordinates three sets of agents: red team agents that map routes to compromise before an attacker walks them, blue team agents that investigate and decide what counts as meaningful risk, and green team agents that take corrective action and harden defences. Microsoft's own description has them handing off to each other automatically rather than parking in a queue for a human between stages. Underneath sits MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, the company's first in-house model built specifically for security work; Microsoft reports its MDASH vulnerability-finding product running on that model at 96 percent on the CyberGym benchmark, twelve points above Anthropic's Claude Mythos, and at close to half the cost of the MDASH configuration Microsoft sells today. Perception is priced as a consumption-based service, which is precisely the question a preview exists to answer: whether the bill stays legible once teams run these loops continuously rather than in demos. Autonomous remediation is staged deliberately, starting with reversible actions such as isolating a machine.

technical.lead: Horizon3 raises 250 million dollars at a valuation above two billion
technical.body: Horizon3 announced a 250 million dollar Series E today at a valuation above two billion dollars, roughly triple the 650 million dollar valuation it carried out of its Series D in June 2025. NightDragon and NEA, both already shareholders, co-led an oversubscribed round that drew seven new investors — Acrew Capital, Blue Cloud Ventures, Demeter Group, Singapore's EDBI, PSG, SAIC and Sapphire Ventures — alongside five returning backers including Qualcomm Ventures and Craft Ventures. NightDragon founder Dave DeWalt, previously chief executive of both FireEye and McAfee, joins the board together with managing director Morgan Kyauk. The company sells an autonomous penetration-testing platform and is pushing from finding weaknesses into remediating them without a human in the loop; it says it approached 100 million dollars in annual recurring revenue last year, growing 120 percent year over year. The pitch it chose for the raise is that offence and defence are now both automated and racing each other, and that framing is what the round prices.

technical.lead: Coding agents rebuilt a CUDA-equivalent stack on d-Matrix in about ten hours
technical.body: Jeremy Nixon, who left Google Brain to found Infinity last year, says his team pointed AI coding agents at d-Matrix silicon and had CUDA-equivalent software running in roughly ten hours, reaching about 92 percent of the Corsair part's theoretical peak on tensor-parallel matrix multiplication across all thirty-two of its compute units. Within ten days, he says, three frontier models were running end to end on the chip with every layer written from scratch. The agent doing the writing is called Ignition; it generates, tests and tunes the compute kernels that decide how efficiently a given accelerator runs a model — historically the work that costs a challenger vendor a specialist team and several years, and the reason porting rarely happens. Two supporting arguments arrived with the claim: Rebellions' Marshall Choy says CUDA no longer factors into inference, and Modular's Chris Lattner likens running AI on CUDA's graphics-inherited stack to squeezing a desktop operating system onto a phone. Against them, Futurum's Daniel Newman points at Nvidia's December purchase of SchedMD, which maintains the Slurm scheduler, and argues the moat got deeper rather than shallower. Infinity closed a 15 million dollar seed at a 100 million valuation last month with OpenAI and Anthropic researchers among the backers, so the claim is early and self-interested — but it is the first version of this argument that comes with a named partner chip and a stopwatch.

technical.lead: Unsloth ships 2026.8.2 to make weight downloads finish, not to add kernels
technical.body: Unsloth published 2026.8.2 to PyPI today, one release after 2026.8.1, with unsloth-zoo moving to the matching version the same day. The substance is not a kernel or a new model family: downloads now fall back automatically from XET to plain HTTP when XET stalls, and memory use during a transfer is much reduced. The team frames it as stability — making a large weight pull finish instead of hanging — which reads as a direct answer to the fetch problems trailing the recent DeepSeek-V4 0731 and Kimi K3 support work rather than as a new capability. The remainder is interface alignment and chat-window fixes. Worth noting for anyone tracking the project by its repository rather than by its package index: the only commits on the main branch today were a merge and a changelog edit, and the release notes for this increment were appended as an August 3 section to the existing beta tag from late July instead of being cut as a fresh one, so PyPI and the changelog are where the version bump is actually visible.
